reason: All key premises are directly and accurately supported by the cited passages from the same 2023 paper (E1, E2, E3), which explicitly describe the SCCP strategy, the resulting strength and ductility values, the mechanism of coherent interfaces, and the compositional/processing requirements. There are no gaps or misrepresentations.
premises: Stepwise thermo-mechanical processing can induce sequential coherent nanoprecipitates (δ-lamella and γ″) in tungsten-based refractory HEAs.
Coherent interfaces of these precipitates facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations, delaying crack initiation.
This microstructure simultaneously increases yield strength (to >2 GPa) and tensile ductility (to ~15%) at ambient temperature.
The alloy retains high yield strength (~1.05 GPa) at 800 °C.
The specific alloy composition (e.g., W1.5Ni2.25Fe with 5 at.% Ta) and controlled processing are required to avoid brittle phases and achieve the desired precipitates.
